candidates.scope: Finite node/occurrence incidence multihypergraph with node bits, alive/fired occurrence flags and explicit optional producer fields, with fixed names or type-respecting bijective renaming
candidates.imageOperation: Typed bipartite incidence graph B with vertex types V/E and edge (v,e) iff v∈ι(e); all node/occurrence attributes retained
candidates.equivalence: encode/decode inverse on named finite states; isomorphism of typed incidence states, not proof of full published graph rewrite theory
candidates.proof: E-side neighborhood of any occurrence vertex exactly reconstructs ι(e); attributes reconstruct labels/statuses; no event occurrence is merged
candidates.negative: Dropping the E partition and taking the pairwise clique loses distinct duplicate hyperedge occurrences

candidates.scope: Fixed finite state, known incidence occurrence set, binary participant bits, alive/unfired flags, common rank k, allowed Hamming weights W
candidates.imageOperation: For each e and S⊆ι(e) with |S|∈W, construct a source-valid reaction (R=S∪{alwaysPresent,alive_e,unfired_e}, I=(ι(e)\S)∪{alwaysAbsent}, P={eligible_e}). The always-present species is in T; always-absent species is not.
candidates.equivalence: Exactly one reaction clause for an occurrence e is enabled iff original En(e), and reaction-system output union equals set of enabled occurrence markers for all e. The extra sentinels ensure source requirement nonempty R, I and P including weights 0 and k.
candidates.proof: R⊆T and I∩T=∅ iff S is exactly the positive-bit subset of ι(e) and e is alive/unfired. That S is unique; it exists among generated clauses iff |S|∈W.
candidates.negative: Native next state is a selected firing with bit mutations, occurrence-state updates, new nodes and child hyperedges, whereas reaction systems fire all enabled products simultaneously and have a fixed species alphabet. Full process equivalence is NOT proved.
candidates.physicalImplication: no inference about underlying chemistry; formal enabling language only

candidates.scope: Fixed finite rank-3 hypergraphs under same named vertices, Carletti hypergraph Laplacian as defined by K_ij=Σ_e(|e|−1)B_eiB_ej
candidates.sourceOperation: Original hypergraph rank-weighted pairwise K and L=D−K operator
candidates.imageOperation: A weighted dyadic graph with edge weights K_ij computes identical selected linear operator for given K
candidates.proof: Two distinct named Fano block collections on V={0,…,6}, each with seven rank-3 hyperedges covering every unordered node pair exactly once, have K_ij=2 for all i≠j and equal L. Under bit1 subset {1,3,5} and native W={3}, an eligible rank3 occurrence appears only in collection A.
candidates.negative: The two collections ARE isomorphic after a simultaneous node permutation. The failure is reconstruction of incidence and named-input guard under fixed labels, NOT unlabeled graph nonisomorphism. The Carletti operator is an observer/selected linear source law, not native bit-rewrite evolution.
candidates.physicalImplication: none established; source physical label preserved only as paper context
